requirements.text: Create the new service as a production, operational, business-critical offering owned by Karen Watkins, positioned as the modern cloud-based successor with improved performance and security
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM service WHERE service_id = 'SVC_049' AND name = 'Next-Gen Customer Experience Platform' AND owned_by = 'USER_039' AND used_for = 'production' AND status = 'operational' AND service_classification = 'business' AND business_criticality = 'critical' AND LOWER(description) LIKE '%cloud%' AND LOWER(description) LIKE '%performance%' AND LOWER(description) LIKE '%security%'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (SVC_049 after SVC_048); the only service the task creates
Karen Watkins is USER_039 on the seed (the acting user, admin, ORG_001)

'business-critical' fixes business_criticality = critical; service_classification = business is read from the same words as the benchmark check does, and in any case is kept from the benchmark check (the legacy service is also classified business)

'positioned as the modern cloud-based successor with improved performance and security' is read as the description, the service's only free-text column, tested by the words cloud, performance and security, case-insensitively; 'successor' is left untested as it may be paraphrased
org_id is not fixed by the request and is not tested

disagreement: description cell form: A 'LOWER(description) LIKE ...' (column repeated in the predicate), B 'LIKE ...'; chose B's form because the README writes a predicate as SQL on the column and the repository's check files write case-insensitive LIKE so, with LOWER() in the sql; same meaning in both passes

requirements.text: Retire the legacy service with clear deprecation messaging
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM service WHERE service_id = 'SVC_005' AND status = 'retired' AND description LIKE '%deprecat%'
assumptions: the legacy service 'NextGen Customer Portal Dev' is SVC_005 on the seed (status non-operational, description 'Sandbox for the new React portal'); anchored by id rather than name so a renamed legacy service still counts

'deprecation messaging' is read as the description mentioning deprecation; '%deprecat%' (SQLite LIKE is case-insensitive) matches every string the benchmark's '%DEPRECATE%' OR '%DEPRECATION%' matches, written as one predicate

requirements.text: including creating a production Customer Self-Service Portal offering owned by Robin Monroe
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM service_offering WHERE service_offering_id = 'SVCOFF_061' AND name = 'Customer Self-Service Portal' AND business_service = 'SVC_049' AND owned_by = 'USER_031' AND used_for = 'production' AND status = 'operational' AND service_classification = 'business' AND business_criticality = 'critical'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (SVCOFF_061 after SVCOFF_060); the only offering the task creates
Robin Monroe is USER_031 on the seed (manager, ORG_001)
the offering belongs to the new platform (business_service = SVC_049): 'migrate ... to the new platform, including creating'

status = operational, service_classification = business and business_criticality = critical kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy (only 'production' is; they mirror the new service)
short_description is NOT NULL in the schema but not fixed by the request; not tested

requirements.text: migrate all associated service offerings to the new platform
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM service_offering WHERE service_offering_id = 'SVCOFF_010' AND business_service = 'SVC_049'
assumptions: the only offering on SVC_005 in the seed is SVCOFF_010 'Portal Dev - UI Sandbox', so 'all associated service offerings' is that one row
migration changes business_service only; the offering's other cells (used_for development, owner) are not fixed by the request and not tested
the new service's id is assumed SVC_049 (next in sequence)

requirements.text: migrate all associated service offerings to the new platform (none left on the legacy service)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM service_offering WHERE business_service = 'SVC_005'
assumptions: migrating is a move, not a copy: one offering (SVCOFF_010) is on the legacy service on the seed, and after migration none may still point at the retired service

requirements.text: ensure all incidents currently linked to the legacy service are updated to reference the new platform
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_011' AND service = 'SVC_049'
assumptions: the only incident with service = SVC_005 in the seed is INC_011 (resolved), so 'all incidents currently linked' is that one row
'reference the new platform' is the incident.service column; INC_011.service_offering (SVCOFF_008, under SVC_004) is not under the legacy service and is not fixed by the request
the new service's id is assumed SVC_049 (next in sequence)

requirements.text: ensure all incidents currently linked to the legacy service are updated to reference the new platform (none left on the legacy service)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE service = 'SVC_005'
assumptions: one incident (INC_011) references the legacy service on the seed; after the update none may

requirements.text: migrate all associated service offerings to the new platform (boundary: only the legacy service's offerings and the new one sit under the new platform)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM service_offering WHERE business_service = 'SVC_049' AND service_offering_id NOT IN ('SVCOFF_010', 'SVCOFF_061')
assumptions: boundary of 'all associated service offerings': only SVCOFF_010 (moved) and SVCOFF_061 (created) may sit under the new platform; this keeps the benchmark's exact count of one migrated offering, which the anchored change requirement on SVCOFF_010 alone does not

disagreement: A has this stay, B does not; kept because it is the boundary of the migration selector (an offering from another service, such as SVCOFF_054 'Guest WiFi - Captive Portal', must not be swept in) and it carries the 'equals 1' part of verify_service_offerings_reassociated

notes: Merged from two passes that agree on all seven benchmark checks (kept) and on seven requirements with the same anchors, selectors, cells and sql: the new service SVC_049 (owned by USER_039 Karen Watkins, with description words cloud, performance, security), the retired legacy service SVC_005 (status retired, description mentioning deprecation), the new offering SVCOFF_061 (owned by USER_031 Robin Monroe, under SVC_049), the migrated offering SVCOFF_010, the two remove requirements (no offering and no incident left on SVC_005) and the incident INC_011 moved to SVC_049; the passes order the requirements differently, which is immaterial. disagreement: the form of the description cells on the new service: A writes 'LOWER(description) LIKE ...', B 'LIKE ...'; chose B's form (the README writes a predicate as SQL on the column, and the repository's check files write case-insensitive LIKE so, with LOWER() in the sql); the meaning is identical, so no value changed (logged on the requirement). disagreement: stay that only SVCOFF_010 and SVCOFF_061 sit under the new platform: A has it, B does not; kept as the boundary of the migration selector and because it carries the exact count of one migrated offering that verify_service_offerings_reassociated tests (logged in the requirement). The passes differ only in wording on why service_classification = business is a cell of the new service (A: kept from the benchmark check, not fixed by the request; B: read from 'business-critical' as the benchmark does); both keep the cell, and the requirement records both readings. Verified on the seed: SVC_005 is the only service whose name contains Customer, Portal, Next or Experience; SVCOFF_010 is the only offering on SVC_005 and the only one whose name contains Customer, Portal or Self apart from SVCOFF_054 'Guest WiFi - Captive Portal' (under SVC_045); INC_011 is the only incident on SVC_005 and no incident references SVCOFF_010; the highest ids are SVC_048 and SVCOFF_060. The benchmark selects the created rows by name; the requirements anchor them by next-in-sequence id, so a tool that numbers ids differently would fail those two requirements but not the benchmark's checks. INC_011 belongs to ORG_002 while the services belong to ORG_001; the request does not address that and it is not tested. The policy (4afd943b) says nothing about services; the acting user is an admin with full CRUD.
